exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Looking for the Lift
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Excuse me, where can I find the lift to the top floor?
Clerk: The lift? Do you mean the elevator, ma'am?
Mia: Oh, yes! In Britain we usually call it the lift.
Clerk: I see. The elevator is just behind the shoe section.
Mia: Thank you. By the way, where do you sell winter boots?
Clerk: They are downstairs, on the first floor.
Mia: The first floor? But this is already the entrance floor.
Clerk: In American English, the first floor is the ground level.
Mia: Ah, that explains it. Thank you for being so patient!
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 问去顶楼的 lift(电梯)在哪;店员问她是不是指 elevator;Mia 说英国人叫 lift;店员指出电梯在鞋区后面;又说冬靴在 first floor(美式指底层),Mia 一度困惑,弄懂后道谢。

questions.stem: What is Mia looking for at first?
options: The lift to the top floor.
The way out of the shop.

questions.stem: What does the American clerk call the lift?
Where is the elevator, according to the clerk?
Where are the winter boots sold?
Why was Mia confused about the 'first floor'?
options: The shop had no first floor.
In American English it means the ground level.
There was no lift at all.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Three Ways to Make Words
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: English makes new words in several simple ways.
One way is to join two words, like 'home' and 'work' into 'homework'.
Another way is to add a prefix or a suffix.
Adding 'un-' to 'happy' gives the opposite, 'unhappy'.
We can also use one word as a different part of speech, such as to 'water' the plants.
exercises.translation_cn: 英语用几种简单方式造新词:一是把两个词合在一起,如 home+work=homework;二是加前缀或后缀,如 happy 加 un- 变 unhappy(相反);三是把一个词用作不同词性,如把名词 water 用作动词'浇水'。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Ways of making new English words.

questions.stem: How is the word 'homework' formed?
What does adding 'un-' to 'happy' do?
options: It makes the word a verb.
It makes the word longer in sound only.

questions.stem: Which is given as the third way to make words?
options: Using one word as a different part of speech.

questions.stem: Which example shows a word used as a verb?

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 What Does BRB Mean?
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Leo: My online friend just typed 'BRB'. What does that mean?
Sara: It means 'be right back'. He'll return in a minute.
Leo: Oh, I thought it was the name of a website!
Sara: No, it's just a short form people use to save time.
Leo: I see. And he often writes 'COZ' too.
Sara: That simply means 'because'. It's quick to type.
Leo: These short forms are clever, but a bit confusing at first.
Sara: True. Just be careful using them with teachers, who may not understand.
exercises.translation_cn: Leo 不懂网友打的 BRB;Sara 解释意思是'马上回来';Leo 以为是网站名;Sara 说只是省时的缩写;Leo 又问 COZ;Sara 说意思是 because;两人说这些缩写聪明但起初令人困惑,对老师用要小心。

questions.stem: What does 'BRB' mean?
What did Leo first think 'BRB' was?
Why do people use these short forms?
What does 'COZ' stand for?
What does Sara warn Leo about?
options: Teachers may not understand these short forms.
The forms are against the law.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 A Crazy Language
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: English can be a really funny language to learn.
There is no ham in a hamburger and no egg in an eggplant.
We sculpt a sculpture, but we simply take a photo.
We feel seasick at sea, yet we are not homesick when we get home.
These surprises show how creative the language can be.
exercises.translation_cn: 英语学起来很有趣:hamburger 里没有 ham,eggplant 里没有 egg;我们 sculpt 出 sculpture,却是 take 一张 photo;在海上 seasick,回到家却不 homesick;这些惊喜说明这门语言很有创造力。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly saying about English?
options: It is the easiest language in the world.
It can be a funny and surprising language.
It is spoken only in Britain.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a hamburger?
options: It is always made with egg.
There is no ham in it.
It is a kind of sculpture.

questions.stem: How do we describe taking a picture?
When do people feel seasick?
What do these surprises show about English?

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Frog in the Throat
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tom: Our teacher Maggie couldn't teach today. She had a frog in her throat.
Ann: A frog in her throat? Did she really swallow a frog?
Tom: No, no. It just means she could hardly speak clearly.
Ann: Oh! So her throat was dry and her voice was weak.
Tom: Exactly. It's a funny English expression.
Ann: English is full of these tricky expressions.
Tom: It is. At first they sound very strange.
Ann: But once you learn the real meaning, they're quite fun.
exercises.translation_cn: Tom 说老师 Maggie 今天不能上课,因为'喉咙里有只青蛙';Ann 以为她真吞了青蛙;Tom 解释那只是说她几乎说不清话;Ann 明白是嗓子干、声音弱;两人感叹英语满是这种棘手却有趣的表达。

questions.stem: Why couldn't Maggie teach that day?
options: She had a frog in her throat.
She had moved to another city.

questions.stem: What did Ann think at first?
options: That Maggie had a pet frog.
That Maggie had really swallowed a frog.

questions.stem: What does the expression really mean?
options: She had caught a real frog.

questions.stem: What do Tom and Ann say about such expressions?
options: They are easy from the start.
They are never used in English.

questions.stem: How does Ann feel once she knows the meaning?
options: She wants to stop learning English.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Choose Your Words Online
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The language we use online is often different from other English.
Short forms and emojis can be quick and clear.
But before you use them, stop and think about your reader.
A teacher may not know what you intend to say.
Make sure your words really suit the situation.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们网上用的语言常和其他英语不同;缩写和表情符号又快又清楚;但用之前先想想读者;老师也许不懂你想表达什么;要确保你的用词真正适合当下情境。

questions.stem: What is the main advice in the passage?
options: Always use as many emojis as possible.
Choose online words that suit your reader and situation.

questions.stem: How does the speaker describe short forms and emojis?
options: They can be quick and clear.
They take a very long time.

questions.stem: What should you do before using them?
options: Send them to everyone at once.
Stop and think about your reader.

questions.stem: Who might not understand your short forms?
What should your words 'really suit'?
